html:
The crucifixion of Jesus was his execution by the Romans outside Jerusalem, most likely in 30 or 33 CE. It is the central event of Christianity, and the cross became its symbol.

According to the four gospels, Jesus came to Jerusalem for the Jewish festival of Passover. After a last meal with his disciples, the Last Supper, he was arrested at night, betrayed by one of them, Judas. He was questioned by the Jewish high priest and council and then handed over to Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judaea under the emperor Tiberius.

Pilate ordered him crucified. Crucifixion was a Roman punishment kept for slaves, rebels and criminals of low status, meant to be slow, painful and public. The charge posted over him was "King of the Jews", which suggests the Romans saw him as a political threat. He was nailed to a cross at a place called Golgotha and died within hours. He was buried in a rock-cut tomb.

Beyond the gospels, the Roman historian Tacitus and the Jewish historian Josephus both mention that he was executed under Pilate. Historians accept the crucifixion as one of the most certain facts about his life.

His followers said that three days later he rose from the dead. For them his death became a sacrifice for the sins of the world, an idea worked out by Paul in his letters. Christians remember the day as Good Friday and celebrate the resurrection at Easter.
sum: The crucifixion of Jesus was his execution by the Romans outside Jerusalem, most likely in 30 or 33 CE. It is the central event of Christianity, and the cross became its symbol.
